title: What is the difference between IEnumerable and IQueryable?
description: Understand deferred execution and query providers.

data.text: **Question:** What is the difference between IEnumerable and IQueryable?

IEnumerable operates on in-memory collections with deferred execution, while IQueryable is designed for remote data sources like databases and can translate queries into the underlying query language (e.g., SQL).

**IEnumerable:**
- Lives in System.Collections.Generic namespace
- Works with in-memory data
- Uses deferred execution but filters happen in memory
- Suitable for LINQ to Objects
- Does not support custom query providers

**IQueryable:**
- Lives in System.Linq namespace
- Extends IEnumerable
- Uses expression trees to represent queries
- Can translate queries to SQL, LDAP, etc.
- Suitable for LINQ to SQL, Entity Framework
- Supports remote query execution

data.title: IEnumerable vs IQueryable

data.caption: IEnumerable filters data in memory after loading everything; IQueryable translates filters to the data source so only matching rows are returned.

Interviewers want to assess:
- Understanding of deferred execution
- Knowledge of expression trees
- Awareness of performance implications
- When to use each interface

items: Not understanding that IQueryable filters are translated to SQL
Mixing IEnumerable and IQueryable causing client-side evaluation
How does LINQ to SQL work internally?

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: IQueryable can translate queries to remote sources
Choose based on data source location
data.takeaway: Use IQueryable for database queries to leverage server-side filtering.
